docs.title: Patchmatic
docs.text: Patchmatic is a macOS application for recording your Eurorack patches — a mix of Modulargrid and VCV Rack without the audio. The name comes from "Patch Schematic"; the original idea was a tool for creating easy-to-read schematics to enable efficient repatching.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
Module design

  • Place knobs, patch points, buttons, toggle switches, sliders, and screens on a panel
  • Adjustable control size, orientation, and label positioning
  • Import a panel photo — controls are detected automatically

Rack assembly

  • Arrange modules in cases with 1U and 3U rows at any HP width
  • Stack multiple cases on a free-form canvas

Patching

  • Draw cables between any two patch points, across cases
  • Physics-based cable rendering with color selection
  • Route cables with intermediate pin points
  • Copy and paste cables between patches on the same rack
  • Add notes to patch points, modules, and patches
  • Group modules with color-coded labels
  • Multiple patches per rack

Sets

  • Organize patches into named, ordered sets for live performance or workflow

Export

  • Print or export patches to PDF

iPad

  • Browse sets on iPad, synced from the Mac through an iCloud Drive folder

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• macOS 14.0 (Sonoma) or later
  • Apple Silicon or Intel
  • iPad app: iPadOS 17.0 or later

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
1. Download Patchmatic-<version>.dmg from the Releases page.
  2. Open the DMG and drag Patchmatic to Applications.
  3. First launch: right-click the app and select Open (the app is not notarized).

Then follow Getting Started.

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text: Patchmatic is organized into four modes, selected from the switcher at the top of the window or with Cmd+1 to Cmd+4. The typical workflow moves through them in order.

docs.title: 1. Create a module
docs.text:
Switch to Modules. Click the camera button in the window toolbar to import a photo of your hardware module; Patchmatic offers to detect its controls automatically. To start from a blank panel, click + instead.

See Module Editor.

docs.title: 2. Build a rack
docs.text:
Switch to Racks. Create a rack, configure its case, and drag modules from the strip at the bottom of the canvas into the rows.

See Rack Editor.

docs.title: 3. Create a patch
docs.text:
Switch to Patches. Click + in the patch list and choose a rack. Drag from one patch point to another to draw a cable.

Each patch stores its own cables, control positions, notes, groups, and screen images.

See Patch Editor.

docs.title: 4. Organize into sets
docs.text:
Switch to Sets to arrange patches into an ordered list and step through them.

See Sets.

docs.title: Saving changes
docs.text:
Edits in Modules, Racks, and Patches mode start an edit session. A Discard Edits / Save Changes bar appears at the bottom of the canvas until you choose one. If you switch to another module, rack, patch, or mode with unsaved changes, Patchmatic asks whether to save or discard them first.

All edits support Undo and Redo (Cmd+Z / Cmd+Shift+Z).

docs.title: Print to PDF
docs.text:
Press Cmd+P (or File > Print Patch…) in Patches or Sets mode to open the print dialog. Use the PDF menu in the dialog to save a PDF instead of printing.

The output includes:

  • The patch name and rack name as a header
  • Patch notes, if any
  • The full rack with every module drawn at its current control values
  • All cables in the patch
  • Patch point sequence numbers, if the Numbers toggle is on
  • Control labels, always shown in print regardless of the Labels toggle
The exported PDF, landscape because the rack is wider than it is tall.

Page orientation is chosen automatically: landscape if the rack is wider than it is tall, portrait otherwise. The content is scaled to fit the page with 18 pt margins.

docs.title: iPad
docs.text: Patchmatic for iPad lets you browse your sets on stage or at the rack. It reads the library from a sync folder in iCloud Drive that the Mac app writes to. The iPad never modifies the library; all editing happens on the Mac.

docs.title: Setting up the sync folder on the Mac
docs.text:
1. Choose File > Sync Folder….
  2. Select a folder in iCloud Drive (the dialog opens there) and click Use Folder.

Patchmatic moves the library into the folder, along with its screen images and audio. If the folder already contains a Patchmatic library, you are asked before it is replaced with the library on the Mac.

While a sync folder is in use, Patchmatic saves to it every 30 seconds when no edit is in progress, so changes reach the iPad without quitting the app.

To keep the library only on the Mac again, choose File > Stop Using Sync Folder. The library, images, and audio are copied back to the Mac's local storage.

Warning

If the sync folder cannot be read at launch, Patchmatic shows a warning and uses the copy stored on the Mac. Changes made in that state do not reach the iPad. Check that iCloud Drive is available, then relaunch or choose the folder again.

docs.title: Connecting the iPad
docs.text:
On first launch, tap Choose Folder and select the same iCloud Drive folder you chose on the Mac. The library loads and the folder is remembered. To switch folders later, tap the folder button at the top of the sidebar.

If the library cannot be loaded, tap Try Again or Choose Another Folder.

The iPad reloads the library automatically when it changes on the Mac, and again when the app returns to the foreground.

docs.title: Browsing sets
docs.text:
The sidebar has two lists:

  • Sets — tap a set to open it
  • Patches in Set — tap a patch to jump to it; patches with an audio preview have a play button

The selected set and patch are remembered on the iPad.

Hide the sidebar to give the rack the full screen. With the sidebar hidden:

  • Swipe in from the left edge of the screen for the previous patch, or from the right edge for the next
  • Dots along the bottom show the position in the set, brightening briefly when the patch changes

docs.title: Viewing a patch
docs.text:
The toolbar has the same Labels, Groups, Numbers, and Notes toggles as the Mac, plus:

  • Frame Rack — fit the rack to the screen. The rack also refits when the iPad rotates or the sidebar is shown or hidden.
  • Display — module image opacity and appearance (System, Light, or Dark)

Pinch to zoom.

Notes — tap a module note or a patch point note dot to read it.

Screen images — tap a screen to open the magnifier, and swipe to page between its images. Tap the magnified image to close it.

Patch notes — the overlay at the top of the canvas shows the patch notes, with a play button when the patch has an audio preview.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• iPadOS 17.0 or later
  • An iCloud Drive folder shared with a Mac running Patchmatic

docs.title: Module Editor
docs.text:
The Module Editor is where you define the layout of individual Eurorack modules. Each module definition is a reusable template that can be placed into any number of racks.

The module library, the panel canvas with its toolbar, and the inspector.

docs.title: Creating a module from a photo
docs.text:
Click the camera button in the window toolbar, drag an image file onto the library, or use Modules > New Module from Image (Cmd+N). Supported formats are PNG, JPEG, TIFF, and HEIC.

Patchmatic creates a new module, sets the photo as its background image, and offers to run automatic control detection. The model identifies knobs, patch points, toggle switches, buttons, and sliders, places them on the panel, and estimates the module's format (1U or 3U) and width in HP.

Review the results after detection — some controls may be missed or misclassified. To re-run detection at any time, click Analyse Background Image in the canvas toolbar, or press Cmd+Shift+A.

Show Detections draws the boxes from the last analysis, color-coded by control type with a confidence score. Hide Controls is turned on here so the photo is visible.

To create a blank module instead, click + or press Cmd+Shift+N.

docs.title: The library
docs.text: Right-click a module in the library for Rename, Duplicate, and Delete. The menu also has an Add to case name submenu for each case in the active rack, listing the rows that match the module's format. Deleting a module that is placed in a rack asks for confirmation first.

docs.title: Module properties
docs.text: Edit the module's name, format (3U or 1U), and width in HP at the top of the inspector. Changing the format rescales the HP width proportionally.

docs.title: The canvas toolbar
docs.text:
From left to right:

Group Buttons Place controls Knob, Patch Point, Toggle Switch, Button, Slider, Screen Background image Set Background Image, Analyse Background Image, Show Detections, Hide Controls Selection Delete Selected Controls, Snap Selected to Grid Alignment Centre Horizontally, Centre Vertically, Distribute Horizontally, Distribute Vertically Grid Show Grid, Grid Divisions (2–128)

docs.title: Adding controls manually
docs.text:
Select a control type in the canvas toolbar to enter placement mode, then click the canvas to place a control. Click the active button again to leave placement mode.

Type Description Knob Rotary control Patch Point 3.5 mm jack Toggle Switch Multi-position switch Button Momentary or latching button Slider Linear fader Screen Rectangular display area

docs.title: Control properties
docs.text:
Select a control to edit it in the inspector. The available properties depend on the control type.

Knob: label, kind, size, and label position. Screen: independent width and height. Button: a separate state label and a list of named states.
  • Size — small, medium, large, or extra large (patch points are always medium)
  • Orientation — vertical or horizontal (toggle switches and sliders)
  • Control Label — position (above, below, left, right, or off), font size, and offset
  • State Label — position, size, and offset of the state name shown for buttons and toggle switches
  • States — named states for buttons and toggle switches; minimum 2, no maximum
  • Width / Height — screens
  • Length — sliders

docs.title: Editing several controls at once
docs.text: With two or more controls selected, the inspector switches to batch editing: a label prefix, kind, size, and label settings applied to every selected control.

docs.title: Selecting and editing controls
docs.text: Action Behaviour Click control Select a single control Shift+Click Add or remove from selection Drag on empty space Pan the canvas Shift+Drag on empty space Marquee selection Click empty space Clear selection Click overlapping controls repeatedly Cycle through the stack Cmd+A Select all controls Cmd+D Duplicate selected controls (offset slightly) Delete Remove selected controls Arrow keys Nudge selected controls 0.5 pt Shift+Arrow keys Nudge 5 pt

docs.title: Resizing controls
docs.text:
Screens and sliders can be resized by dragging a handle on their selection highlight:

Control Handle location Resizes Screen Bottom-right corner Width and height Horizontal slider Right edge Length Vertical slider Bottom edge Length

docs.title: Alignment and grid
docs.text:
• Snap Selected to Grid — moves the selected controls to the nearest grid intersection. The grid cell size is the shorter side of the panel divided by Grid Divisions.
  • Show Grid — draws the grid over the panel.
  • Centre Horizontally / Vertically — aligns the selection to its average position (2+ controls).
  • Distribute Horizontally / Vertically — spaces controls evenly between the two outermost (3+ controls).

docs.title: Background image
docs.text: The imported photo sits behind the controls. Use the Image Opacity slider in the window toolbar to fade it while positioning controls. To replace the photo without re-running detection, click Set Background Image in the canvas toolbar.

docs.title: Canvas navigation
docs.text:
• Scroll wheel or pinch — zoom (1×–8×)
  • Option+Drag or drag on empty space — pan
  • Zoom In / Zoom Out — toolbar buttons or Cmd+= / Cmd+-
  • Frame — reset zoom and centre the view (Cmd+0)

docs.title: Saving
docs.text: Any change starts an edit session with a Discard Edits / Save Changes bar at the bottom of the canvas. Saving a module that is placed in a rack asks for confirmation, then updates every placement.

docs.title: Patch Editor
docs.text: A patch is a snapshot of a rack: it stores cable connections, control positions, notes, groups, and screen images independently from every other patch on the same rack. You can have as many patches per rack as you like.

docs.title: Toolbar
docs.text:
Toggle Action Labels Show or hide control labels Groups Show or hide group overlays and the group list Numbers Show or hide patch point sequence numbers Notes Show or hide the patch notes overlay

The toolbar also has zoom in, zoom out, frame to fit, and the module image opacity slider.

docs.title: Creating, duplicating, and deleting patches
docs.text:
Click + in the patch list, or use Patches > New Patch, and choose a rack from the submenu.

Right-click a patch in the list for Rename, Patch Notes…, Duplicate, and Delete…. Duplicating (Cmd+D) copies the cables, control values, screen images, notes, groups, patch notes, and audio.

Deleting a patch asks for confirmation, and warns if the patch will also be removed from any sets. Deletion can be undone with Edit > Undo, which restores the patch and its place in each set.

docs.title: Drawing cables
docs.text:
Drag from one patch point to another. A preview cable follows the pointer, and the cable is created when you release over a valid patch point. Colors are assigned automatically from a 24-color palette in rotation.

To change a cable's color, right-click it and choose Change Color.

Right-clicking a cable selects it and opens its menu.

docs.title: Selecting cables
docs.text:
• Right-click a cable to select it and show its context menu
  • Shift+Click a cable to add it to or remove it from the selection
  • Shift+Drag to draw a marquee; every cable it touches is added to the selection (when the Groups toggle is off)
  • Right-click a patched patch point to select all of its cables and show the cable menu
Shift+Drag selects every cable the rectangle touches.

docs.title: Deleting cables
docs.text:
Delete the selected cables with the Delete key or Delete Selected Cables in the cable menu.

The canvas context menu also has a Delete Cable submenu listing every cable by its endpoints, in the form "Module Jack → Module Jack". A patch point without a label is shown by its sequence number.

docs.title: Copying and pasting cables
docs.text:
Copy the selected cables with Cmd+C, Copy Selected Cables in the cable menu, or Patches > Copy Cables. Paste with Cmd+V, Paste Cables in the canvas or cable menu, or Patches > Paste Cables.

Cables can only be pasted into a patch on the rack they were copied from. Pasted cables become the selection. Cables whose modules are no longer in the rack, or that duplicate an existing connection, are skipped.

docs.title: Routing cables with pins
docs.text:
Pins are waypoints that redirect a cable's path.

  • Cmd+Click a cable, or choose Add Cable Pin in its menu, to add a pin
  • Drag a pin to move it
  • Right-click a pin and choose Delete Cable Pin, or select it and press Delete

Pins attached to a case move with the case.

docs.title: Adjusting controls
docs.text:
• Knobs — drag vertically (up increases, down decreases)
  • Sliders — drag along the slider
  • Toggle switches and buttons — click to step to the next named state

All control values are stored per patch.

docs.title: Screen images
docs.text:
Hover over a screen to show its toolbar:

  • + — attach an image
  • Magnifier — show the current image enlarged
  • Trash — delete the current image
  • ← / → — cycle through images, when a screen has more than one

Attaching an image opens a dialog. By default the whole image is used. Check Crop Image to show a crop rectangle, and Lock Aspect Ratio to keep it to the screen's shape.

Cropping a module photo to just its display.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
Patch point notes — right-click a patch point with no cables and choose Add Patch Point Note or Edit Patch Point Note. A dot marks the patch point; hover over it to read the note.

Module notes — right-click the module body (not over a patch point) and choose Add Note to place a free-form note on the panel.

Both kinds of note are stored per patch.

docs.title: Groups
docs.text:
Groups color-highlight sets of modules. Turn on the Groups toggle to show the overlays and the floating group list.

Groups and Numbers turned on. Hovering a group card highlights its modules.

With the Groups toggle on:

  • Create a group — right-click a module and choose New Group with name. Shift+Right-click to add more modules to the selection first.
  • Add or remove modules — right-click a module and use Add to Group or Remove from Group
  • Hover a group card — highlights that group's modules and fades the rest
  • Click a group card — frames the group's modules
  • Right-click a group card — rename, edit notes, or delete the group

docs.title: Patch notes
docs.text:
Each patch has free-form notes and an optional audio preview. The notes appear in an overlay at the top of the canvas when the Notes toggle is on, Hover over the overlay to show a play button when audio is attached.

Click the overlay, choose Patch Notes… from the canvas or patch list menu, or use Patches > Patch Notes… to edit them. Attach Audio Preview adds an audio file to the patch.

docs.title: Canvas navigation
docs.text:
• Scroll wheel or pinch — zoom (0.25×–5.0×)
  • Drag on empty space — pan
  • Frame to Fit — fits all cases to the viewport (Cmd+0 or toolbar button)

docs.title: Saving
docs.text: Changes start an edit session with a Discard Edits / Save Changes bar at the bottom of the canvas.

docs.title: Rack Editor
docs.text:
The Rack Editor is where you assemble module definitions into a physical case layout.

A case with one 1U row and two 3U rows. Modules are dragged in from the strip at the bottom.

docs.title: Racks and cases
docs.text:
A rack is a top-level container that holds one or more cases. Cases represent physical enclosures; several cases in one rack model a multi-case setup as a single unit.

To create a rack, click + in the rack list (or Cmd+N). To add a case, click New Case in the toolbar, press Cmd+Shift+C, or right-click empty canvas space. New cases start with two rows.

New Case, Labels, zoom and frame, and module image opacity.

docs.title: Configuring a case
docs.text:
• Rename — click the case name in its header
  • HP width — click the HP value in the header; it applies to every row in the case
  • Add a row — click the gear in the header (or right-click the case) and choose Add 3U Row or Add 1U Row
  • Remove a row — the same menu, Remove Row; this also removes the modules in that row

docs.title: Placing modules
docs.text:
Drag a module thumbnail from the module strip onto a row. A dashed outline shows the target position while dragging.

Placement rules:

  • A 3U module can only go in a 3U row, and a 1U module in a 1U row
  • The row must have enough free HP at the drop position

You can also right-click a module in the Module Editor library and use Add to case name.

To remove a module, select it and press Delete, or right-click it and choose Delete.

docs.title: Moving modules
docs.text:
Drag a placed module to move it. Modules snap to the HP grid and can be dragged to another row or another case.

If you drag a single module onto modules already in a row, they are pushed aside to make room: modules whose centre is left of the dragged module move left, the rest move right. The new positions are previewed while you drag. The move is only allowed if the row has enough free HP in total.

Dragging Ts-L into uO_c's position pushes uO_c to the right.

Select several modules with Shift+Click or a marquee drag, then drag one of them to move them all. A multi-module move stays within its case.

Use the Left and Right arrow keys to nudge selected modules by 1 HP.

docs.title: Arranging cases on the canvas
docs.text: Drag a case by its header to reposition it on the canvas. Guide lines appear when a case aligns with another, and cases snap to an 8 HP grid while dragging. Selecting several cases and dragging one moves them together.

docs.title: Canvas navigation
docs.text:
• Scroll wheel or pinch — zoom (0.25×–5.0×)
  • Drag on empty space — pan
  • Frame to Fit — fits all cases to the viewport (Cmd+0 or toolbar button)

Zoom and pan position are saved between sessions.

docs.title: Saving
docs.text: Any change starts an edit session with a Discard Edits / Save Changes bar at the bottom of the canvas. If the rack has patches, saving asks for confirmation first.

docs.title: Sets
docs.text: A set is an ordered list of patches — a live performance running order, or a sequence of related configurations to step through.

docs.title: Creating a set
docs.text: In Sets mode, click + in the set list (or Cmd+N). Right-click a set to rename or delete it.

docs.title: Adding and ordering patches
docs.text:
The patches in the selected set are listed below the set list. Click Add Patch at the bottom of the sidebar and pick a patch; the menu lists the patches that are not already in the set. A patch can belong to any number of sets.

A speaker icon marks the patch currently shown.

Drag a patch row to reorder it. To remove a patch from the set, right-click it and choose Remove from Set — the patch itself is not deleted.

docs.title: Stepping through a set
docs.text: Use the Left / Right arrow keys (or Cmd+← / Cmd+→), or the buttons in the bar at the bottom of the canvas. The bar shows the position and the current patch name. Clicking a patch in the list jumps straight to it.

docs.title: Read-only canvas
docs.text:
The canvas in Sets mode is read-only: cables cannot be created or deleted, controls cannot be adjusted, and no context menus appear. The patch notes overlay can still be clicked to read the notes for the current patch.

To change a patch, edit it in Patches mode and return to Sets.

Sets can also be browsed on an iPad — see iPad.

docs.title: Global
docs.text: Shortcut Action Cmd+1 Switch to Modules mode Cmd+2 Switch to Racks mode Cmd+3 Switch to Patches mode Cmd+4 Switch to Sets mode Cmd+Z Undo Cmd+Shift+Z Redo Cmd+= Zoom in Cmd+- Zoom out Cmd+0 Frame to fit Cmd+Shift+L Toggle labels Cmd+P Print / export to PDF

docs.title: Modules Mode
docs.text: Shortcut Action Cmd+N New module from image Cmd+Shift+N New blank module Cmd+R Rename module Cmd+D Duplicate module (library) / duplicate selected controls (canvas) Delete Delete selected module(s) (library) / delete selected control(s) (canvas) Cmd+Shift+A Analyse background image Cmd+A Select all controls Arrow keys Nudge selected controls 0.5 pt Shift+Arrow keys Nudge selected controls 5 pt

docs.title: Racks Mode
docs.text: Shortcut Action Cmd+N New rack Cmd+R Rename rack Cmd+Shift+C New case Cmd+D Duplicate rack Cmd+A Select all modules Delete Remove selected modules or cases Left / Right Arrow Nudge selected module(s) ±1 HP

docs.title: Patches Mode
docs.text: Shortcut Action Cmd+R Rename patch Cmd+D Duplicate patch Delete Delete selected cables or pin Cmd+C Copy selected cables Cmd+V Paste cables Shift+Click cable Add or remove cable from selection Shift+Drag Marquee-select cables Cmd+Click cable Insert cable pin at click location

docs.title: Sets Mode
docs.text: Shortcut Action Cmd+N New set Cmd+R Rename set Left Arrow / Cmd+← Previous patch in set Right Arrow / Cmd+→ Next patch in set
